subject: dlply, dropping columns, equivalence classes, and other good stuff

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: dlply, dropping columns, equivalence classes, and other good stuff
parts:
It might be nice to have an option for dropping the columns by which you're splitting.

Currently, I can do that using something like this:

Define example:

xx <- data.frame(a=LETTERS[1:8],b=rep(1:2,each=1),c=rep(1:2,each=2),d=rep(1:2,each=4))

For one variable:

> dlply(xx,.(b),function(q){q[,"b"]<-NULL;q})
$`1`
  a c d
1 A 1 1
2 C 2 1
3 E 1 2
4 G 2 2

$`2`
  a c d
1 B 1 1
2 D 2 1
3 F 1 2
4 H 2 2

attr(,"split_type")
[1] "data.frame"
attr(,"split_labels")
  b
1 1
2 2

For n variables, a little messier:

> vars <- c("b","d")
> dlply(xx,vars,function(q){q[,vars]<-rep(list(NULL),length(vars));q})})
$`1.1`
  a c
1 A 1
2 C 2

$`1.2`
  a c
1 E 1
2 G 2

$`2.1`
  a c
1 B 1
2 D 2

$`2.2`
  a c
1 F 1
2 H 2

attr(,"split_type")
[1] "data.frame"
attr(,"split_labels")
  b d
1 1 1
2 1 2
3 2 1
4 2 2

But this seems pretty clumsy. How about something like dlply(xx,vars,..., .coldrop=TRUE) ?

The motivation for this case was that I was splitting up a data frame by each different column, and then wanted to divide the resulting subframes into equivalence classes to see the mapping from variables to number of equivalence classes:

> xx <- data.frame(a=rep(LETTERS[1:4],2),
                   b=rep(1:2,each=1),
                   c=rep(1:2,each=2),
                   d=rep(1:2,each=4))
> llply(names(xx),
        function(col) { z <- dlply(xx,col,
                                   function (q) { q[,col]<-NULL ; q });
                        match(z,unique(z))
                      }
)

[[1]]           <<< I'd like this to be labelled 'a'
[1] 1 2 3 4     <<< 4 equivalence classes

[[2]]
[1] 1 2

[[3]]
[1] 1 2

[[4]]
[1] 1 1          <<< down to 1

Of course, if people have better suggestions on how to do this (the equivalence classes), I'd be interested.

Also, why doesn't llply have the same names/attributes as dlply, namely attr(,"split_labels")?

For that matter, how can I name the list elements? Do I have to explicitly do zzz <- llply(...); names(zzz) <- names(xx) ) ?

          -s

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: dlply, dropping columns, equivalence classes, and other good stuff
parts:
I'll answer the easy part. The reason you're not getting a named list
out of llply is that the list you put in doesn't have names. You can
do

xxn <- names(xx)
names(xxn) <- xxn

llply(xxn, ...

to keep the names in the resulting list.

Best,
Ista
